en: 8. Cittayamaka 8.1.
Uddesa 8.1.1.
Commonality of Pure Consciousness (Suddhacittasāmañña)
8.1.1.1. Chapter on Persons (Puggalavāra) 8.1.1.1.1.
Chapter on the Distinction of the Times of Arising and Cessation Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
For whom the mind arises but does not cease, will that person’s mind cease but not arise?
Or conversely, for whom the mind will cease but not arise, does that person’s mind arise but not cease?
For whom the mind does not arise but ceases, will that person’s mind not cease but arise?
Or again, for that person whose consciousness will cease and will arise, does his consciousness not arise and cease?
8.1.1.1.2. Chapter on Arising and Aroused:
For that person whose consciousness arises, has his consciousness arisen?
Or again, for whomsoever consciousness has arisen, does consciousness arise for that person?
For whomsoever consciousness does not arise, has consciousness not arisen for that person?
Or again, for whomsoever consciousness has not arisen, does consciousness not arise for that person?
8.1.1.1.3. Section on Cessation and Arising For whom consciousness ceases, for that person does consciousness arise?
Or, conversely, for whom consciousness arises, for that person does consciousness cease?
For whom consciousness does not cease, for that one does consciousness not arise?
Or else, for whom consciousness does not arise, for that one does consciousness not cease?
8.1.1.1.4. The Chapter on Arising (Uppādavāra).
For whom consciousness arises, for that one has consciousness arisen?
Or rather, for whom consciousness has arisen, for that one does consciousness arise?
For whom consciousness does not arise, for that one has consciousness not arisen?
Or again, for whom mind had not arisen, does mind not arise for that person?
For whom mind arises, will mind arise for that person?
Or again, for whom mind will arise, does mind arise for that person?
For whom consciousness does not arise, for that person will consciousness not arise?
Or conversely, for whom consciousness will not arise, for that person does consciousness not arise?
For whom consciousness has arisen, for that person will consciousness arise?
Or again, for whomsoever consciousness will arise, for that person has consciousness arisen?
For whomsoever consciousness has not arisen, for that person will consciousness not arise?
Or again, for whomsoever consciousness will not arise, for that person has consciousness not arisen?
8.1.1.1.5. Section on Cessation (Nirodhavāra) For whom the consciousness ceases, for that person did the consciousness cease?
Or conversely, for whom the consciousness had ceased, for that person does the consciousness cease?
For whom consciousness does not cease, for that person has consciousness not ceased?
Or conversely, for whom consciousness has not ceased, for that person does consciousness not cease?
For whom consciousness ceases, for that person will consciousness cease?
Or, for whomsoever the mind will cease, does the mind cease for that person?
For whomsoever the mind does not cease, will the mind not cease for that person?
Or, for whomsoever the mind will not cease, does the mind not cease for that person?
For whom consciousness has ceased, will consciousness cease for that person?
Or conversely, for whom consciousness will cease, has consciousness ceased for that person?
For whom consciousness has not ceased, will consciousness not cease for that person?
Or, for whomsoever the consciousness will not cease, for that person did the consciousness not cease?
8.1.1.1.6. Chapter on Arising and Cessation:
For whomsoever the consciousness arises, for that person did the consciousness cease?
Or, for whomsoever consciousness had ceased, does consciousness arise for that person?
For whomsoever consciousness does not arise, had consciousness not ceased for that person?
Or, for whomsoever consciousness had not ceased, does consciousness not arise for that person?
Does the consciousness that arises in a person necessarily cease?
Or, conversely, does the consciousness that will cease in a person necessarily arise?
Does the consciousness that does not arise in a person necessarily not cease?
Or again, for whomsoever the consciousness will not cease, does that consciousness not arise?
For whomsoever consciousness had arisen, will that consciousness cease?
Or again, for whomsoever consciousness will cease, had that consciousness arisen?
For whom consciousness has not arisen, will that consciousness not cease?
Or, for whom consciousness will not cease, had that consciousness not already arisen?
8.1.1.1.7. The Section on Arising and Ceasing.
For whom consciousness arises, for that one does consciousness not cease?
Or rather, for whom consciousness does not cease, for that one does consciousness arise?
For whom consciousness does not arise, for that one does consciousness cease?
Or, for whomsoever the consciousness ceases, does the consciousness not arise for that person?
8.1.1.1.8. The Chapter on the Arising and the Aroused:
For whomsoever the consciousness is arising, is the consciousness aroused for that person?
Or, for whomsoever the mind has arisen, for that one is the mind arising?
For whomsoever the mind is not arising, for that one is the mind not arisen?
Or, for whomsoever the mind is not arisen, for that one is the mind not arising?
8.1.1.1.9. Section on the Ceasing and Arising [of Consciousness] For whom consciousness is ceasing, for that person is consciousness arisen?
Or conversely, for whom consciousness is arisen, for that person is consciousness ceasing?
For whom the consciousness is not ceasing, for that person is the consciousness not arisen?
Or else, for whom the consciousness is not arisen, for that person is the consciousness not ceasing?
8.1.1.1.10. Chapter on the Arisen and the Arousing.
For whom consciousness has arisen, for that one has consciousness arisen?
Or rather, for whom consciousness has arisen, for that one has consciousness arisen?
For whom consciousness has not arisen, for that one has consciousness not arisen?
Or, for whomsoever consciousness had not arisen, has consciousness not arisen for him?
For whomsoever consciousness has arisen, will consciousness arise for him?
Or, for whomsoever consciousness will arise, has consciousness arisen for him?
For whom the consciousness has not arisen, will that consciousness not arise?
Or, conversely, for whom the consciousness will not arise, has that consciousness not arisen?
8.1.1.1.11. Chapter on the Past and Future.
For whom mind had arisen but mind has not [now] arisen, will mind arise for that person?
Or again, for whom mind will arise but mind has not [now] arisen, had mind arisen for that person?
For whom mind had not arisen and mind has not [now] arisen, will mind not arise for that person?
Or, for whomsoever the consciousness will not arise, yet for whom that consciousness has not [already] arisen, has that consciousness not already arisen for him?
8.1.1.1.12. Chapter on the Arisen and the Arising:
That which has arisen is [also] arising?
Is that which is arising already arisen?
Is it neither arisen nor arising?
Is it neither arising nor arisen?
8.1.1.1.13. The Section on the Ceased and the Being Ceased:
Is that which has ceased the same as that which is being ceased? Is that which is being ceased the same as that which has ceased?
Not ceased, not ceasing? Not ceasing, not ceased?
8.1.1.1.14. The Section on the Time Transcended.

Is the mind of one whose mind, while arising, has transcended moment by moment and transcended its time, also that mind of one whose mind, while ceasing, has transcended moment by moment and transcended its time?

Or conversely, is the mind of one whose mind, while ceasing, has transcended moment by moment and transcended its time, also that mind of one whose mind, while arising, has transcended moment by moment and transcended its time?

Is that consciousness of one whose consciousness, while arising, has transgressed moment by moment and passed beyond time; and whose consciousness, while ceasing, has transgressed moment by moment and passed beyond time?

Or conversely, is that consciousness of one whose consciousness, while ceasing, has transgressed moment by moment and passed beyond time; and whose consciousness, while arising, has transgressed moment by moment and passed beyond time?
8.1.1.2. Section on Phenomena (Dhammavāra)
8.1.1.2.1. Section on the Conjunction of the Times of Arising and Cessation Is that consciousness which is arising and not ceasing the same as that consciousness which will cease and will not arise?
Or, conversely, is that consciousness which will cease and will not arise the same as that consciousness which is arising and not ceasing?
That consciousness which does not arise and does not cease—will that consciousness not cease and will it arise?
Or, conversely, that consciousness which will not cease and will arise—does that consciousness not arise and not cease?
8.1.1.2.2. Chapter on Arising and Aroused.
Is that consciousness which arises that consciousness which has arisen?
Or, conversely, is that consciousness which has arisen that consciousness which is arising?
Is that consciousness which does not arise that consciousness which has not arisen?
Or again, whatever consciousness has not arisen, does that consciousness not arise?
8.1.1.2.3. Chapter on Cessation and Arising: Whatever consciousness ceases, does that consciousness have arisen?
Or again, is that consciousness which has arisen ceasing?
Is that consciousness which is not ceasing unarisen?
Or again, is that consciousness which is unarisen not ceasing?
8.1.1.2.4. Section on Arising (Uppādavāra): Whatever consciousness arises, has that consciousness already arisen?
Or, whatever consciousness has already arisen, is that consciousness arising?
Is that consciousness which does not arise that consciousness which did not arise?
Or rather, is that consciousness which did not arise that consciousness which does not arise?
Is that consciousness which arises that consciousness which will arise?
Or again, is that consciousness which will arise [now] arising?
Is that consciousness which is not arising not going to arise?
Or again, is that consciousness which will not arise not arising?
Whatever consciousness had arisen, will that consciousness arise?
Or else, whatever consciousness will arise, had that consciousness already arisen?
Whatever consciousness had not arisen, will that consciousness not arise?
Or, whatever consciousness will not arise, has that consciousness not arisen? 8.1.1.2.5.
Chapter on Cessation (Nirodhavāra):
Whatever consciousness ceases, has that consciousness ceased?
Or rather, is that consciousness which has ceased the same consciousness that is ceasing?
Is that consciousness which is not ceasing the same consciousness that has not ceased?
Or rather, is that consciousness which has not ceased the same consciousness that is not ceasing?
Is that consciousness which is ceasing also about to cease?
Or, conversely, is that consciousness which is about to cease also ceasing?
Is that consciousness which is not ceasing also not about to cease?
Or again, is that consciousness which will not cease not ceasing?
Is that consciousness which has ceased about to cease?
Or again, is that consciousness which will cease having ceased?
Whatever consciousness has not ceased, will that consciousness not cease?
Or, whatever consciousness will not cease, has that consciousness not ceased? 8.1.1.2.6.
Chapter on Arising and Cessation.
Does that consciousness which arises have ceased?
Or, conversely, does that consciousness which has ceased arise?
Does that consciousness which does not arise not cease?
Or rather, is that consciousness which has not ceased not arising?
Is that consciousness which is arising about to cease?
Or rather, is that consciousness which is about to cease arising?
Is that consciousness which does not arise not to cease?
Or conversely, is that consciousness which will not cease not arising?
Is that consciousness which has arisen to cease?
Or else: whatever consciousness will cease, had that consciousness arisen?
Whatever consciousness had not arisen, will that consciousness not cease?
Or else: whatever consciousness will not cease, had that consciousness not arisen?
8.1.1.2.7. Section on Arising and Ceasing Does that consciousness which is arising not cease?
Or, conversely, does that consciousness which does not cease arise?
Does that consciousness which does not arise cease?
Or conversely, does that consciousness which ceases not arise? 8.1.1.2.8.
The Chapter on Arising and Appeared Consciousness.
Is that consciousness which is arising that consciousness which has arisen?
Or, conversely, is that consciousness which has arisen that consciousness which is arising?
Is that consciousness which is not arising that consciousness which has not arisen?
Or, is that consciousness which has not arisen also not arising?
8.1.1.2.9. The Chapter on the Ceasing and Arising of Consciousness: Is that consciousness which is ceasing also arisen?
Or, is that consciousness which has arisen also ceasing?
Is that consciousness which is not ceasing also not arisen?
Or, is that consciousness which is not arisen also not ceasing?
8.1.1.2.10. Section on the Arisen and the Arousing Is that consciousness which has arisen that consciousness which had already arisen?
Or, conversely, is that consciousness which had already arisen that consciousness which has arisen?
Is that consciousness which has not arisen that consciousness which has not already arisen?
Or conversely, is that consciousness which has not already arisen that consciousness which has not arisen?
Is that consciousness which has arisen that consciousness which will arise?
Or again, is that consciousness which will arise already arisen?
Is that consciousness which has not arisen not going to arise?
Or again, is that consciousness which will not arise not already arisen?
8.1.1.2.11. Section on the Past and Future (Atītānāgatavāra) That consciousness which had arisen but has not [yet] arisen—that consciousness will it arise?
Or, that consciousness which will arise but has not [yet] arisen—had that consciousness already arisen?
That consciousness which had not arisen, yet is not non-arisen—that consciousness will it not arise?
Or else, that consciousness which will not arise, yet is not non-arisen—that consciousness had it not arise?
8.1.1.2.12. The Chapter on the Arisen and the Arising.
Is that which has arisen also arising?
Is that which is arising already arisen?
Is there that which is neither arisen nor arising?
Is it not arising and not arisen?
8.1.1.2.13. The Chapter on the Ceased and the Ceasing:
Is it ceased and ceasing?
Is that which is ceasing already ceased?
Is it not ceased and not ceasing?
Is it not ceasing and not ceased?

8.1.1.2.14. Section on Exceeded Time (Atikkantakālavāra) Whatever consciousness, while arising, exceeds moment after moment and thus has exceeded its time—is that consciousness [the same as] whatever consciousness, while ceasing, exceeds moment after moment and thus has exceeded its time?

Or conversely, whatever consciousness, while ceasing, exceeds moment after moment and thus has exceeded its time—is that consciousness [the same as] whatever consciousness, while arising, exceeds moment after moment and thus has exceeded its time?

Is that consciousness which has passed beyond each moment of its arising—that is, has transcended the time of arising—not that consciousness which has passed beyond each moment of its ceasing—that is, has transcended the time of ceasing?

Or conversely, is that consciousness which has passed beyond each moment of its ceasing—that is, has transcended the time of ceasing—not that consciousness which has passed beyond each moment of its arising—that is, has transcended the time of arising?
8.1.1.3. Section on Persons and Phenomena (Puggaladhammavāra)
8.1.1.3.1. Section on the Distinction of the Times of Arising and Cessation For whomsoever a certain consciousness arises and does not cease, will that consciousness cease for him and not arise?
Or, conversely, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will cease and not arise, does that consciousness arise and not cease for him?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness does not arise and ceases, will that consciousness for him not cease and arise?
Or conversely, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will not cease and will arise, does that consciousness for him not arise and cease?
8.1.1.3.2. Chapter on Arising and Aroused.
For whomsoever a certain consciousness arises, does that consciousness arise for them?
Or conversely, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has arisen, does that consciousness arise for them?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness does not arise, does that consciousness not arise for them?
Or conversely, for whatever person a certain consciousness has not arisen, does that consciousness not arise for that person?
8.1.1.3.3. Chapter on Cessation and Arising:
For whatever person a certain consciousness ceases, has that consciousness arisen for that person?
Or rather, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has arisen, does that consciousness cease for him?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness does not cease, has that consciousness not arisen for him?
Or rather, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has not arisen, does that consciousness not cease for him?
8.1.1.3.4. Section on Arising (Uppādavāra) For whomsoever a certain consciousness arises, for that person did that consciousness arise previously?
Or conversely, for whomsoever a certain consciousness arose previously, for that person does that consciousness arise [now]?
For whom that consciousness does not arise, for them has that consciousness not arisen?
Or conversely, for whom that consciousness has not arisen, for them does that consciousness not arise?
For whom that consciousness arises, for them will that consciousness arise?
Or rather, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will arise, does that consciousness arise for them?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness does not arise, will that consciousness not arise for them?
Or rather, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will not arise, does that consciousness not arise for them?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness has arisen, will that same consciousness arise for them?
Or conversely, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will arise, had that same consciousness already arisen for them?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness has not arisen, will that same consciousness not arise for them?
Or conversely, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will not arise, had that consciousness not already arisen for them?
8.1.1.3.5. Chapter on Cessation (Nirodhavāra):
For whomsoever a certain consciousness ceases, had that consciousness already ceased for them?
Or again, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has ceased, does that consciousness cease for them?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness does not cease, has that consciousness not ceased for them?
Or again, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has not ceased, does that consciousness not cease for them?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness ceases, will that same consciousness cease for him?
Or rather, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will cease, does that same consciousness cease for him?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness does not cease, will that same consciousness not cease for him?
Or rather, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will not cease, does that consciousness not cease for him?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness has ceased, will that consciousness cease for him?
Or rather, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will cease, has that consciousness ceased for him?
For whom that consciousness did not cease, for them will that consciousness not cease?
Or rather, for whom that consciousness will not cease, for them did that consciousness not cease?
8.1.1.3.6. Section on Arising and Cessation.
For whomsoever a certain consciousness arises, does that consciousness cease for that person?
Or rather, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has ceased, does that consciousness arise for that person?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness does not arise, does that consciousness not cease for that person?
Or, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has not ceased, does that consciousness not arise for him?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness arises, will that consciousness cease for him?
Or, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will cease, does that consciousness arise for him?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness does not arise, will that consciousness not cease for them?
Or conversely, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will not cease, does that consciousness not arise for them?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness has arisen, will that consciousness cease for them?
Or again, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will cease, has that consciousness arisen for him?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness has not arisen, will that consciousness not cease for him?
Or again, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will not cease, has that consciousness not arisen for him?
8.1.1.3.7. Section on Arising and Ceasing For whom a certain consciousness arises, does that consciousness not cease for that person?
Or conversely, for whom a certain consciousness does not cease, does that consciousness arise for that person?
For whom that consciousness does not arise, for that person does that consciousness cease?
Or conversely, for whom that consciousness ceases, for that person does that consciousness not arise?
8.1.1.3.8. The Chapter on Arising and Appeared Consciousness.
For whomsoever a certain consciousness is arising, for that person is that consciousness arisen?
Or conversely, for whomsoever a certain consciousness is arisen, for that person is that consciousness arising?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness is not arising, for that person is that consciousness not arisen?
Or conversely, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has not arisen, has that consciousness not yet arising for him?
8.1.1.3.9. The Chapter on the Ceasing and the Arising:
For whomsoever a certain consciousness is ceasing, has that consciousness already arisen for him?
Or, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has arisen, is that consciousness of his ceasing?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness is not ceasing, is that consciousness of his not arisen?
Or, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has not arisen, is that consciousness of his not ceasing?
8.1.1.3.10. Section on the Arisen and the Arousing (Uppannuppādavāra) For whomsoever a certain consciousness has arisen, for that person has that consciousness already arisen?
Or conversely, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has already arisen, for that person has that consciousness arisen?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness has not arisen, for that person has that consciousness not arisen in the past?
Or conversely, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has not arisen in the past, for that person has that consciousness not arisen [now]?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness has arisen, for that person will that consciousness arise [in the future]?
Or again, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will arise, has that consciousness already arisen for him?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness has not arisen, will that consciousness not arise for him?
Or again, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will not arise, has that consciousness not already arisen for him?

8.1.1.3.11. Section on the Past and Future (Atītānāgatavāra) For whomsoever a certain consciousness has arisen, but that consciousness has not yet appeared [in the present], will that consciousness arise for him?
Or conversely, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will arise, but that consciousness has not yet appeared, had that consciousness already arisen for him?
For whom that consciousness had not arisen, and for whom that consciousness has not [yet] arisen, will that consciousness not arise for them?
Or rather, for whom that consciousness will not arise, and for whom that consciousness has not [yet] arisen, had that consciousness not already arisen for them?
8.1.1.3.12. Chapter on the Arisen and the Arising (Uppannuppajjamānavāra)
Is that which has arisen also arising?
Is that which is arising already arisen?
Is there that which is neither arisen nor arising?
Is that which is not arising not arisen?
8.1.1.3.13. Chapter on the Ceased and the Ceasing:
Is that which has ceased ceasing?
Is that which is ceasing already ceased?
Is it not ceased and not ceasing?
Is it not ceasing and not ceased?

8.1.1.3.14. Section on Exceeded Time (Atikkantakālavāra) For whatever consciousness, when arising, exceeds moment by moment and has exceeded its time, and when ceasing, exceeds moment by moment and has exceeded its time—is that consciousness [exceeded] for that person?

Or conversely, for whatever consciousness, when ceasing, exceeds moment by moment and has exceeded its time, and when arising, exceeds moment by moment and has exceeded its time—is that consciousness [exceeded] for that person?
For whomsoever a certain consciousness has not transgressed the moment-by-moment arising and has passed beyond the time of arising, does that consciousness belong to him?
Or conversely, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has not transgressed the moment-by-moment ceasing and has passed beyond the time of ceasing, does that consciousness belong to him?
